h1: The 6 Best Bagged Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six bagged upright and canister vacuums compared on filtration, tools, weight and pet-friendly disposal for 2026.
summary: The Kenmore 81414 is the best bagged vacuum, a HEPA canister with an extended telescoping wand, retractable cord and four tools. The Kenmore 81214 keeps HEPA and a two-motor system for less. The Oreck Commercial XL is the light upright, the Intuition Hair Eliminator targets long hair, the Lift-Up handles stairs, and the Eureka 3670H is the budget canister.
intro: A bagged vacuum earns its place at the moment you empty it. A bin has to be dumped into the trash, throwing a puff of fine dust back into the room, while a bag lifts out sealed and goes in the bin whole. For allergy households that single difference outweighs a lot of marketing. The catch is that not every bag system is good: filtration and the tool kit decide how much of that sealing advantage you keep.

Six models made the cut, three Kenmore bagged designs among them. We compared them on paper, using spec sheets and listings, on HEPA filtration, tool count, reach, body type and weight, and gave prices as buckets because retail numbers move. Only two of the six actually claim HEPA, which shapes the top of the list.

products.name: Kenmore 81414 400 Series Pet Friendly Lightweight Bagged Canister Vacuum with Extended Telescoping Wand, HEPA, Retractable Cord, and 4 Cleaning Tools
products.verdict: The most complete bagged canister in this group.
products.description:
The Kenmore 81414 is the complete bagged package. Its HEPA filtration holds fine particles inside the machine instead of returning them to the air, and an extended telescoping wand plus a retractable cord handle the logistics. Four cleaning tools cover stairs, upholstery and ceiling corners, which is where a bagged canister is better than any upright. It sits in the $200 to $500 bracket, the highest here.

It leads because the tool count and wand reach mean you will not need extras. The 81214 below shares HEPA but ships with one fewer tool, no telescoping wand listed, and costs less.

Buy it for pet households with mixed floors and stairs. The caveat is body type: a canister has to be dragged behind you, and in a home that is mostly wall-to-wall carpet an upright makes the work quicker.
products.idealFor: Pet households with mixed floors and stairs.

products.name: Kenmore 81214 200 Series Pet Friendly Lightweight Bagged Canister Vacuum with HEPA, 2 Motor System, and 3 Cleaning Tools
products.verdict: HEPA and a two-motor design without the premium price.
products.description:
The Kenmore 81214 is the value play. It carries HEPA filtration, a two-motor system and three cleaning tools, in the $100 to $200 range. A second motor is the spec to check on a canister, because carpet pickup is where single-motor models tend to feel underpowered.

It ranks second since you lose a tool and the extended wand compared with the 400 Series, but keep the filtration and the dual-motor design. For most buyers the saved money matters more than the telescoping reach.

Choose it if you want HEPA and strong suction without the top price, especially for allergies. The caveat is height: the listing shows no telescoping wand, so cleaning tall spaces, ceiling corners or high shelves is harder than with the 81414.

products.name: Oreck Commercial XL Vacuum Cleaner, Bagged Upright Vac, Lightweight
products.verdict: A light, durable upright for people who dislike lugging a canister.
products.description:
The Oreck Commercial XL is a different philosophy: a lightweight bagged upright with commercial-grade construction, in the $100 to $200 bracket. A light body is the point. Pushing a heavy upright around a whole floor tires you, and this one invites quick, frequent passes.

It sits third because the spec sheet shows no HEPA claim and no tool kit, so it trails the two Kenmore canisters on filtration and versatility. What you get in exchange is a simple machine that is easy to push and built to take wear.

Buy it for quick, regular cleaning of carpets and hard floors where durability counts. The caveat is attachments: do not expect upholstery or crevice tools, and for allergy-sensitive homes the missing HEPA label makes the Kenmore 81214 a safer purchase for similar money.

products.name: Kenmore Intuition Bagged Upright Vacuum with Hair Eliminator Brushroll
products.verdict: Targets the tangled brushroll that ruins other uprights.
products.description:
The Kenmore Intuition with the Hair Eliminator brushroll is aimed at one problem: hair wrapped tight around the roller. Long hair and pet fur wind around a plain brushroll until it stalls, and you cut it free with scissors. This bagged upright is built to reduce that wrap, and it costs in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It ranks fourth because it lacks a listed HEPA claim and tool kit, so it is a narrower product than the canisters above. The brushroll is what separates it from the Lift-Up Intuition below, and it suits hair-heavy homes better.

Pick it if tangles are the chore you resent. The caveat is the missing detail: no HEPA label and no tool listing means you cannot count on filtration or attachment, so allergy households should look at the 81214 first.
products.idealFor: Homes with long hair or shedding pets.

products.name: Kenmore Intuition Bagged Upright Vacuum Lift-Up Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: An upright that lifts off for stairs, no canister needed.
products.description:
The Lift-Up Intuition solves the oldest complaint about uprights: stairs. The cleaning section detaches from the body, so you can carry the head up a flight or hold it against upholstery without hauling the whole machine. It is a bagged upright in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It sits behind the Hair Eliminator model since stairs are a narrower need than tangled brushrolls, but it fills a real gap that plain uprights cannot. The canisters above handle stairs too, with more reach and tools.

A multi-level carpeted home is the right fit. The caveat is limited information: the listing offers little detail, with no HEPA claim, so check the wand length before relying on it for tall dusting. Skip it if your house has no stairs.

products.name: Eureka Bagged Canister Vacuum Cleaner, 3670H
products.verdict: Canister reach for the least money here.
products.description:
The Eureka 3670H is the cheapest way into a bagged canister, at $50 to $100. It includes replacement bags in the box, and a canister gives you the reach for stairs and under furniture that a basic upright cannot match. Starting with spare bags avoids an early reorder.

It comes last because the listing gives no filtration or tool details. You are buying the form factor and the entry price, not a documented feature set, and the Kenmore canisters list HEPA and tool counts.

It suits apartments and second-floor vacuums that rarely see heavy use. The caveat is capability: for a pet household or any allergy concern, the missing HEPA claim and thin feature list point you to the Kenmore 81214. Expect fewer attachments, and verify the bag style number before reordering.

whatMatters.detail: A HEPA filter traps very fine particles that ordinary filters release back into the room, which matters most for allergies and pets. A bagged design only keeps that advantage if the exhaust air is filtered too, so the filter spec matters as much as the bag. Look for the exact word HEPA in the title or bullets, not a vague claim of allergen filtering.

Uprights are fast on carpet and store standing, while canisters reach stairs, furniture and ceilings more easily and drag behind you. The right body depends on your floors and storage. Consider whether you clean mostly big open rooms or awkward spots like stairs, and check the listing for wand length if you choose an upright model.

A bagged vacuum needs bags that fit its specific model, and the supply is part of the cost. Check that replacements are easy to buy, compare prices for a multipack, and confirm the style number printed in the manual. A listing that includes spare bags, like the Eureka 3670H, saves an early reorder and a wait.

Hair wraps around a plain brushroll and forces you to stop and cut it free. A Hair Eliminator style design reduces that wrap. If you have long hair or shedding pets, look for the term in the product title, and not just a general claim about pet suction, since only the Intuition lists it.

Crevice tools, dusting brushes and upholstery heads are what make a canister useful beyond floors. Count the tools in the title or bullets, since the Kenmore 81414 lists four and the 81214 lists three. A telescoping wand extends reach to ceiling corners and high shelves, and a retractable cord saves time between rooms.

faq.q: Are bagged vacuums better than bagless?
faq.a: They seal dust inside until you dispose of the bag, which is cleaner for allergies than dumping a bin. The tradeoff is buying bags, and a HEPA bagged model like the Kenmore 81414 adds filtration that most bagless budget models skip.

faq.q: Do all of these use HEPA?
faq.a: Only the Kenmore 81414 and 81214 list HEPA. The Oreck, the two Intuition uprights and the Eureka 3670H do not claim it, so allergy households should treat their filtration as unconfirmed and ask before buying.

faq.q: How often should I change the bag?
faq.a: Change it when it is roughly full, since a packed bag cuts airflow and strains the motor. Many owners swap it when suction drops, and the Eureka comes with replacement bags so you can start right away.

faq.q: Is an upright or canister better for stairs?
faq.a: A canister such as the Kenmore 81414 or the Intuition Lift-Up works best on stairs. Both let you hold the cleaning head off the machine and reach each step, while a standard upright is awkward and heavy to lift.
No. Bags are model-specific, so confirm the style number printed in the manual or on the listing before you order. A wrong-fit bag defeats the point of buying bagged.

faq.q: Is the Eureka 3670H enough for a pet home?
faq.a: Likely for light use, but the Kenmore canisters offer HEPA and more tools. A pet home with shedding hair benefits from the 81214's two-motor system, so spend a bit more if the budget allows and shedding is a daily fact of life.

finalTake: Buy the Kenmore 81414 for pets, mixed floors and the full tool kit, or the 81214 to keep HEPA and save money. Choose the Oreck for light, frequent floor work, the Hair Eliminator upright for tangles and the Lift-Up for carpeted stairs. The Eureka suits apartments and occasional use, not allergy homes.
